facts.text: The opt-in Pi-in-Tern runner `.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` feeds stdin through pi-tui's `StdinBuffer` and dispatches each complete sequence via `keyEffect`, so raw character handling no longer treats a Kitty CSI-u ESC prefix as Escape.

In `.pi/lib/tern/run.ts`, `StdinBuffer` emits `paste` events to `bridge.pasteText`, and `pasteText` in `.pi/lib/tern/bridge.ts` replaces newlines with spaces for non-large pastes, so embedded newlines do not submit.
The TSP surface credit gate blocks new frames when unacknowledged frames reach the credit limit, and no window drawing the pane means acks stop, so credits cannot advance until the window is focused.

The Pi-in-Tern prototype is opt-in: it runs only by launching `node --experimental-strip-types .pi/lib/tern/run.ts` in a Tern pane, and the default Pi CLI has not been replaced. OMP visual parity and a model-driven live prompt remain unverified.

The untracked Code Puppy Tern plugin scaffold in `tern-plugins/code-puppy/` defines a `code-puppy.status` block (`host.luau`) and Start/Status/Interrupt/Stop palette commands (`window.luau`); its README says full chat and approvals are not covered by this plugin alone.

`.pi/lib/tern/tsp.ts` `diffChildren`/`diffNode` diffs keyed nodes into `del`, `add`, `text append`, and `set` ops, so only changed parts are sent; `TernInlineSurface.#flush` remains credit-gated, and `bridge.ts` owns the composer dock and transcript frames.

The Code Puppy Python plugin in `tern-plugins/code-puppy/python-plugin/register_callbacks.py` registers a `render_final_response` callback that claims the `agent_response` banner and returns `{"handled": True}`; other results or exceptions leave Rich output in place, and the first claim wins.

The Code Puppy Python plugin is installed manually by symlinking `tern-plugins/code-puppy/python-plugin` to `~/.code_puppy/plugins/tern`; Code Puppy's `_load_user_plugins` then imports its `register_callbacks.py` at startup.
